encyclopedia.name: Compsognathus
encyclopedia.description: About the size of a chicken! Compsognathus was one of the smallest dinosaurs — about the size of a chicken! But it was a fierce little predator.

encyclopedia.name: Velociraptor
encyclopedia.description: About the size of a turkey Velociraptors were actually only about the size of a turkey, not the giant creatures shown in movies!

encyclopedia.name: Stegosaurus
encyclopedia.description: As long as a bus! Stegosaurus had a brain the size of a walnut, but it had bony plates on its back that could flush with blood to regulate body temperature.

encyclopedia.name: Triceratops
encyclopedia.description: Heavy as an elephant! Triceratops' frill wasn't just for protection — scientists think it was used to attract mates, like a peacock's tail!

encyclopedia.name: T-Rex
encyclopedia.description: Tall as a giraffe!

encyclopedia.name: Brachiosaurus
encyclopedia.description: Could peek into a 4th-floor window! Brachiosaurus could eat leaves from trees up to 30 feet high — that's like eating off the roof of a three-story building!

encyclopedia.name: Argentinosaurus
encyclopedia.description: Heavier than 14 elephants combined! The Argentinosaurus was so massive it weighed about 100 tons — that's heavier than 14 African elephants combined!

encyclopedia.name: Ankylosaurus
encyclopedia.description: The Ankylosaurus had a tail club so powerful it could break the bones of a T-Rex. Talk about a built-in weapon!

encyclopedia.name: Giganotosaurus
encyclopedia.description: The Giganotosaurus from South America had a skull over 5 feet long — one of the biggest heads ever on a land predator!

encyclopedia.name: Dreadnoughtus
encyclopedia.description: Dreadnoughtus, meaning 'fears nothing', was one of the most massive land animals ever — weighing about 65 tons!

encyclopedia.name: Diplodocus
encyclopedia.description: Diplodocus could crack its tail like a whip, creating a sonic boom that could be heard from miles away!

encyclopedia.name: Megalosaurus
encyclopedia.description: The first dinosaur fossil ever scientifically described was Megalosaurus in 1824, by William Buckland in England.

encyclopedia.name: Tyrannosaurus Rex
encyclopedia.description: T-Rex had the strongest bite of any land animal ever — about 12,800 pounds of force! That's like having a small car dropped on you. Some scientists believe T-Rex had feathers — at least as a baby. Imagine a fluffy T-Rex chick!

encyclopedia.name: Pteranodon
encyclopedia.description: Pterodactyls weren't actually dinosaurs! They were flying reptiles called pterosaurs that lived alongside dinosaurs.

encyclopedia.name: Spinosaurus
encyclopedia.description: Spinosaurus is the largest known carnivorous dinosaur, even bigger than T-Rex! It was also a fantastic swimmer.

encyclopedia.name: Micropachycephalosaurus
encyclopedia.description: The Micropachycephalosaurus has the longest name of any dinosaur — try saying that five times fast!

encyclopedia.name: Parasaurolophus
encyclopedia.description: Parasaurolophus had a long hollow crest on its head that it could use like a trumpet to make deep, booming sounds!

encyclopedia.name: Oviraptorosaur
encyclopedia.description: Some dinosaur eggs were as big as footballs! The largest ever found belonged to a type of oviraptorosaur.

encyclopedia.name: Utahraptor
encyclopedia.description: The Utahraptor was the largest raptor dinosaur, about 23 feet long and 1,100 pounds. Now THAT's a raptor!

encyclopedia.name: Pachycephalosaurus
encyclopedia.description: Pachycephalosaurus had a skull dome 10 inches thick! Scientists debate whether they head-butted each other like rams.

encyclopedia.name: Quetzalcoatlus
encyclopedia.description: The Quetzalcoatlus had a wingspan of 36 feet — as wide as a small airplane! It was the largest flying animal ever.

encyclopedia.name: Therizinosaurus
encyclopedia.description: Therizinosaurus had claws up to 3 feet long — the longest claws of any animal that ever lived!

encyclopedia.name: Iguanodon
encyclopedia.description: Iguanodon was one of the first three dinosaurs ever named, and scientists originally put its thumb spike on its nose like a horn!

fossilData.name: Tyrannosaurus Rex Skull
fossilData.funFact: T-Rex had forward-facing eyes, giving it excellent depth perception for hunting!

fossilData.name: Triceratops Horn
fossilData.funFact: Each horn could be up to 3 feet long — longer than a baseball bat!

fossilData.name: Raptor Claw
fossilData.funFact: The sickle-shaped claw was used for pinning down prey, not slashing!

fossilData.name: Stegosaurus Plate
fossilData.funFact: The plates weren't attached to the skeleton — they grew in the skin!

fossilData.name: Sauropod Vertebra
fossilData.funFact: A single neck vertebra could be over 3 feet long!

fossilData.name: Pteranodon Wing Bone
fossilData.funFact: Despite its huge wingspan, Pteranodon only weighed about 55 pounds!

fossilData.name: Ankylosaur Tail Club
fossilData.funFact: The tail club was made of fused bones and could swing with 500 pounds of force!

fossilData.name: Dinosaur Egg
fossilData.funFact: Oviraptor means 'egg thief' but it was actually protecting its OWN eggs!

discoveryData.name: Hell Creek Formation
discoveryData.description: One of the most famous fossil sites in the world, where the first well-preserved T-Rex was found.

discoveryData.name: Flaming Cliffs
discoveryData.description: Where the first dinosaur eggs were discovered in 1923, changing our understanding of dinosaur reproduction.

discoveryData.name: Patagonia
discoveryData.description: Home to the largest dinosaurs ever discovered, including the massive Argentinosaurus.

discoveryData.name: Dinosaur Provincial Park
discoveryData.description: UNESCO World Heritage Site with over 40 dinosaur species found — one of the richest fossil beds on Earth!

discoveryData.name: Solnhofen Limestone
discoveryData.description: Where the first Archaeopteryx was found — the missing link between dinosaurs and birds!

discoveryData.name: Lyme Regis
discoveryData.description: Mary Anning's legendary fossil hunting grounds, where she discovered complete marine reptile skeletons as a teenager!

discoveryData.name: Morrison Formation
discoveryData.description: The site of the great 'Bone Wars' between rival paleontologists Cope and Marsh in the 1870s!

discoveryData.name: Liaoning Province
discoveryData.description: Revolutionary feathered dinosaur fossils found here proved the dinosaur-bird connection beyond doubt!

discoveryData.name: Tendaguru
discoveryData.description: Africa's richest dinosaur fossil site, where the massive Giraffatitan skeleton was excavated.

discoveryData.name: Ischigualasto
discoveryData.description: Known as 'Valley of the Moon' — home to some of the oldest dinosaurs ever found, from the very dawn of the age of dinosaurs!

discoveryData.name: Narmada Valley
discoveryData.description: India's dinosaur country! The fierce Rajasaurus — 'King Lizard' — was discovered here, a uniquely Indian predator.

discoveryData.name: Ariyalur
discoveryData.description: A treasure trove of fossils in Southern India — the Bruhathkayosaurus found here may have been one of the largest dinosaurs ever!

quizQuestions.question: Which dinosaur had the strongest bite force of any land animal?
quizQuestions.explanation: T-Rex had a bite force of about 12,800 pounds — enough to crush bone!

quizQuestions.question: How big was a real Velociraptor?
quizQuestions.explanation: Velociraptors were actually only about the size of a turkey — not the giants shown in movies!

quizQuestions.question: Which dinosaur had plates on its back that could regulate body temperature?
quizQuestions.explanation: Stegosaurus plates could flush with blood to help cool down or warm up!

quizQuestions.question: What does the word 'dinosaur' mean in Greek?
quizQuestions.explanation: Dinosaur means 'terrible lizard' — but they weren't actually lizards at all!

quizQuestions.question: Which period did dinosaurs first appear?
quizQuestions.explanation: Dinosaurs first appeared during the Late Triassic, about 230 million years ago.

quizQuestions.question: How many horns did Triceratops have?
quizQuestions.explanation: Triceratops means 'three-horned face' — two long brow horns and one shorter nose horn!

quizQuestions.question: What are the closest living relatives of dinosaurs?
quizQuestions.explanation: Birds evolved from small theropod dinosaurs and are technically dinosaurs themselves!

quizQuestions.question: How wide was the asteroid that wiped out the dinosaurs?
quizQuestions.explanation: The Chicxulub asteroid was about 6 miles wide — roughly the size of Mount Everest!

quizQuestions.question: Which of these was the largest flying animal ever?
quizQuestions.explanation: Quetzalcoatlus had a wingspan of 36 feet — as wide as a small airplane!

quizQuestions.question: Where was the Rajasaurus dinosaur discovered?
quizQuestions.explanation: Rajasaurus — meaning 'King Lizard' — was discovered in India's Narmada Valley!

dinoGlossary.definition: An extinct marine animal with a spiral shell, common fossils from the Mesozoic Era.
An animal that walks on two legs, like T-Rex and Velociraptor.
A meat-eating animal. Many theropod dinosaurs were fierce carnivores.
Fossilized dinosaur poop! Scientists study these to learn what dinosaurs ate.
The last period of the Mesozoic Era (145–66 million years ago). Ended with the asteroid impact.
The scientific name for the group of all dinosaurs, coined by Richard Owen in 1842.
When every member of a species dies out. Non-bird dinosaurs went extinct 66 million years ago.
Preserved remains or traces of ancient life found in rock. Can be bones, teeth, footprints, or even eggs!
Stones swallowed by dinosaurs to help grind food in their stomachs — like a built-in blender!
A plant-eating animal. Sauropods and ceratopsians were herbivores.
A marine reptile that looked like a dolphin. Not a dinosaur, but lived alongside them!
The middle period of the Mesozoic Era (201–145 million years ago). The age of giant sauropods!
The geological boundary marking the mass extinction event 66 million years ago that ended the dinosaurs.
The 'Age of Reptiles' — the era spanning 252–66 million years ago, divided into Triassic, Jurassic, and Cretaceous.
An animal that eats both plants and meat. Some dinosaurs like Oviraptor were likely omnivores.
A scientist who studies ancient life through fossils. They're real-life dinosaur detectives!
Flying reptiles that lived alongside dinosaurs. They were NOT dinosaurs, but close relatives!
An animal that walks on four legs, like Triceratops and Stegosaurus.
Short for dromaeosaurid — a family of feathered, fast-running predatory dinosaurs.
Giant long-necked, plant-eating dinosaurs like Brachiosaurus and Argentinosaurus — the largest land animals ever!
Two-legged, mostly carnivorous dinosaurs. Includes T-Rex, Velociraptor, and modern birds!
The first period of the Mesozoic Era (252–201 million years ago). When dinosaurs first appeared!
A single bone in the spine. Some sauropod vertebrae were over 3 feet long!

events.title: First Dinosaurs
events.desc: Small, bipedal dinosaurs like Eoraptor appear in what is now Argentina.

events.title: Rise of Theropods
events.desc: Herrerasaurus and other early predators begin to diversify.

events.title: End-Triassic Extinction
events.desc: Volcanic eruptions wipe out many species, allowing dinosaurs to dominate.

events.title: Dinosaurs Dominate
events.desc: With competitors gone, dinosaurs become the rulers of the land.

events.title: Giants Emerge
events.desc: Brachiosaurus, Diplodocus, and other massive sauropods roam the Earth.

events.title: Stegosaurus Era
events.desc: Plated dinosaurs with spiked tails thrive in lush forests.

events.title: First Birds
events.desc: Archaeopteryx — half dinosaur, half bird — takes flight in Germany.

events.title: Feathered Dinosaurs
events.desc: Sinosauropteryx and other feathered species discovered in China.

events.title: Flowering Plants
events.desc: The first flowers appear, transforming ecosystems worldwide.

events.title: Spinosaurus
events.desc: The largest known carnivore — bigger than T-Rex — hunts fish in rivers.

events.title: Triceratops Appears
events.desc: Three-horned giants roam North America in vast herds.

events.title: T-Rex Reigns
events.desc: The most famous predator of all time dominates the Late Cretaceous.

events.title: The Asteroid Impact
events.desc: A 6-mile-wide asteroid strikes the Yucatán Peninsula. The age of dinosaurs ends.

events.title: Birds Survive
events.desc: Small feathered dinosaurs survive the extinction — evolving into today's birds.
